title: Automatically Archive Amazon EBS Snapshots with Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager
content:
Automatically Archive Amazon EBS Snapshots with Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager Customers utilize snapshots to capture a point-in-time copy of their data, enabling disaster recovery, migrating data across regions and accounts, and enhancing backup compliance. For enterprises that rely on snapshots, there is often a need to retain snapshots that are infrequently accessed for more than 90 days for compliance reasons. However, the cost associated with storing these full snapshots for prolonged periods poses a challenge to IT budgets, leading to potential non-compliance as customers may feel pressured to delete snapshots due to financial constraints.
On November 29, 2021, Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) introduced the Amazon EBS Snapshots Archive, a new storage tier designed for the long-term retention of Amazon EBS snapshots of EBS volumes. We are thrilled to announce that customers can now utilize Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager – a policy-based lifecycle management solution for EBS Snapshots and EBS-backed Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) at no additional cost – to establish custom policies that automate the archival and retention of EBS Snapshots.
In this workshop, we explore how to use Data Lifecycle Manager to automate the creation, archival, and deletion of Amazon EBS Snapshots. Customers who need to maintain full, point-in-time snapshots for backup and compliance purposes can now achieve this through ‘set-and-forget’ policies, eliminating the need for complex custom scripts that could result in data loss due to human errors.

title: Introduction
content: Introduction In this workshop, we’ll demonstrate two methods of automating snapshot archival and management using Data Lifecycle Manager. Additionally, we’ll provide instructions on utilizing the EC2 Console to observe the snapshots managed and archived by Data Lifecycle Manager. The first method involves establishing an age-based policy for automating the creation and archival of snapshots through a singular policy schedule. The second method introduces a strategy to automate snapshot creation and archival across multiple policy schedules. One schedule is designed to maintain daily/weekly snapshots within the Amazon EBS Snapshot Standard tier, whereas another schedule is tasked with transferring snapshots generated on a monthly basis to the EBS Snapshots Archive tier.

title: Launch EC2 Instance
content:
Launch EC2 Instance   In the AWS Management Console, navigate to and select EC2.
  Within the EC2 console, click on Instances.
 Then, click on Launch instances.    On the Launch Instances page:
 Specify Name and tags as FCJ Snapshot.    Under Key Pair, you may select Proceed without a key pair (Not recommended).
 For Networking, retain the default configuration.    For Storage, maintain the default settings and then click on Launch instance.
  Once the EC2 instance is launched, click on View all instances.
  Allow approximately 2 minutes for the instance to initialize. Wait until the Status check shows 2/2 checks passed.
  Select the newly created instance, navigate to Storage, and then click on Volume.
  Assign the volume tag as FCJ-Volume.

title: Preparation
content:
Preparation We will prepare an EC2 instance for use in subsequent steps.
 Launch an EC2 instance

title: Using a Single Policy Schedule
content:
Use a Policy Schedule   Access the EC2 Console
 Navigate to the Lifecycle Manager. Click on Next step.    In the Settings Step, Target Resources
 For Target resource type, choose Volume. Filter by tags, specifically FCJ-Volume.    Utilize the Default IAM Role
  Proceed by Selecting Next
  Configure the Schedule
 This step involves setting up one schedule and one policy. In the Schedule name field, enter a name of your choice. For Frequency, select Daily. Under Every, choose 1 hour. Set Starting at to 14:00 or adjust as needed. For Retention type, select 30 days.    Review the Policy
  Create the Policy
  Lifecycle Policy Created Successfully

title: Use multiple policy schedules
content:
Use multiple policy schedules   Same, but we will create multiple policy schedules with 1 policy lifecycle.
 In the Data Lifecycle Manager console Select Create lifecycle policy     Select EBS snapshot policy
 Select Next     For Target resource, select Volume
 Select by tag: FCJ-Volume Set description as FCJ-DLM-Week policy     Use default IAM Role.
 Select Next.     Go to Schedule configuration step
 For Schedule name, enter optionally. Select Frequency as Weekly Choose the dates of your choice. Choose starting at time as 09:00 For Retention type, select Age and select 180 days    Select Add another schedule   Perform the 2nd Schedule Configuration
 For Schedule name, enter optionally. Select Frequency as Monthly Select Day and Last Choose starting at time as 09:00 For Retention type, select Age and select 1 days    Select Advanced settings   For Snapshot archiving
 Select Archive snapshots created by this schedule Archive snapshots for 90 days Select Review policy    Check again and select Create policy  Finish creating lifecycle policy

title: Review results
content: Review the result.  We review the results by going to the EC2 console and selecting Snapshots  Select a snapshot and view the details.  Select Tags to view detail information about schedule policy and data lifecycle policy

title: Clean up resources
content:
Clean up resources   Deleting lifecycle policy
 Select the policy. Select Actions. Select Delete lifecycle policy.    Confirm deletion.   Choose to delete snapshots.
 Select snapshots related to the lab. Select Actions. Select Delete snapshot.    Confirm deletion.   Implement Terminate EC2 instance.
 Select EC2 instance. Select Instance state. Select Terminate instance.
